Items.Authors: Shubhendra Nath Das, Kapil Kumar Bharadwaj, Abhijit Chakraborty, Kevikumar Ashokbhai Lad, Jajaendra Siva Seshu Vera Prasad Neelam, Rishikesh Sharma, Nikitha Jitendran, Vishal Joshi
Items.Title: Design and development of Fabry-Perot based wavelength calibration system for PARAS-2 spectrograph
Items.Abstract: Detecting Earth-sized and sub-Neptune exoplanets demands sub–meter-per-second RV precision, requiring highly stable wavelength calibration. Traditional hollow cathode lamps (ThAr, UAr, UNe) suffer from uneven line spacing, blends, and aging effects, while laser frequency combs, though extremely stable, remain costly and complex. Fabry–Perot (FP) etalons offer an affordable alternative with dense, uniformly spaced, high-SNR lines.  We report the development and initial performance of a custom FP wavelength calibrator for the PARAS-2 spectrograph on the PRL 2.5-m telescope. Built with a 5-mm Corning ULE spacer, it provides a free spectral range of ~0.03 nm at 550 nm and over 10,000 lines across 400–690 nm. After accounting for the instrumental profile, the finesse ranges from ~7 to ~11. With temperature stability of 0.002 °C and pressure stability of 5×10⁻⁴ mbar, the system achieves a theoretical RV stability better than 10 cm/s per night.

Items.Authors: Ran Duan, Hanzhang Wang
Items.Title: Design and electromagnetic optimization of aluminum kinetic inductance detectors for 850 GHz astronomical observations
Items.Abstract: Targeting potential future 850 GHz ground-based facilities in China, we present the design of Aluminum LEKID arrays. Utilizing high-fidelity Sonnet simulations incorporating complex superconducting surface impedance, we optimized the pixel geometry on high-resistivity silicon. A key focus is mitigating electromagnetic crosstalk in high-density arrays required for these envisioned observatories. We rigorously investigate architectural solutions, specifically staggered pixel arrangements and inter-pixel ground shielding. Simulation results confirm significant isolation improvements. Future work will focus on fabrication and cryogenic characterization to experimentally validate the electromagnetic models. This work lays the technical groundwork for conceptual sub-millimeter instrumentation.

Items.Authors: Diana Dimitrova, Robert Daniel Parsons, Marek Kowalski, David Berge
Items.Title: Design and verification of a simultaneous 4 channel CMOS system
Items.Abstract: Wide-field optical surveys such as LSST, ZTF, Pan-STARRS, and the upcoming ULTRASAT, are designed to periodically image large portions of the sky to detect and characterize transient objects. Each night, these surveys provide thousands of new sources making high cadence follow-up increasingly important. To address this, we have developed a cost-effective multi-channel optical follow-up system, using an off-the-shelf telescope and mount, commercial dichroic beamsplitters and components, enabling significant cost reduction through scaling. Initial observations show that the system is performing as expected, with depth limited by light-pollution rather than hardware. We have demonstrated that in proper observing conditions, the system can reach within 240s exposure time using a single telescope, the same limiting magnitudes as the ZTF. Multiple telescopes can be combined in an array to increase depth and surveying speed.

Items.Authors: Jian-Rong Gao, B. Mirzaei, M. Finkel, C. Walker, Jian-Rong Gao
Items.Title: Design of a 2.7 THz dual-polarized quasi-optical HEB mixer
Items.Abstract: We design a 2.7-THz dual-polarized antenna in a novel configuration that feeds four hot-electron bolometers (HEBs) through coplanar-waveguide (CPW) transmission lines. The antenna performance is modeled using COMSOL Multiphysics, and its far-field beam pattern is analyzed when combined with an elliptical lens. The resulting dual-polarized, quasi-optical HEB mixer is suitable for supra-THz frequencies (>1 THz), as required for spaceborne heterodyne receivers to improve signal-to-noise ratio, and thus observing efficiency with minimal added complexity.

Items.Authors: Yuxin Qiu, Hanzhang Wang, Ran Duan, Shiling Yu, Xiaoyun Ma, Ruirui Fan, Nannan Yue, Xaojing Wu, Wei Duan
Items.Title: Design of a compact multi-layer kinetic inductance detector for high pixel density imaging arrays
Items.Abstract: The design of a high-pixel-density Kinetic Inductance Detector (KID) array for near-to-mid infrared imaging is presented. To improve the low filling factor of traditional designs, a compact architecture based on multi-layer Parallel Plate Capacitors (PPCs) is proposed. Using vertical stacking and interconnects with a thin amorphous silicon dielectric, a pixel pitch of less than 100 μm is achieved. Uniquely, the capacitor layer functions as a backshort to enhance optical absorption. Simulations show high quality factors (Q~50,000) with controlled crosstalk. Additionally, a Strip Modular Structure is introduced to improve manufacturing yield for large-scale arrays, and strategies to mitigate Two-Level System (TLS) noise are discussed.

Items.Authors: Boon-Kok Tan, Peter K. Day
Items.Title: Design of a kinetic-inductance impedance-matched parametric amplifier using an inverted microstrip architecture
Items.Abstract: Josephson parametric amplifiers (JPAs) are key tools in superconducting quantum electronics but are inherently narrow band. While travelling-wave parametric amplifiers broaden bandwidth significantly, they require long nonlinear transmission lines or large junction arrays. An alternative approach, the impedance-matched parametric amplifier (IMPA), uses passive resonators to extend bandwidth, though most implementations rely on SQUID-based nonlinearity.    We present a kinetic-inductance IMPA (KIMPA) using niobium titanium nitride employing an inverted microstrip rather than a coplanar waveguide, reducing vulnerability to shorts, improving mechanical robustness, and enabling compact parallel-plate capacitors. Using a graph-based filter-synthesis model and harmonic-balance simulations, we predict a broadband gain profile demonstrating the viability of this architecture.

Items.Authors: Xiaolan Huang, Shibo Shu, Feng Liu, Sunil R. Golwala, Miao Li
Items.Title: Design of a six-band, 2.4-octave (80--420 GHz) hierarchically summed phased-array slot-dipole antenna array for NEW-MUSIC
Items.Abstract: The Next-generation Extended Wavelength Multi-band Sub/millimeter Inductance Camera (NEW-MUSIC) is the first six-band trans-millimeter wave polarimeter mounted on the Leighton Chajnantor Telescope (LCT). To realize this innovative instrument, we propose a broadband, hierarchical phased-array antenna integrated with band-defining filters, covering a wide spectral range of 80~420 GHz (2.4 octaves). This design enables key scientific investigations, including studies of trans-millimeter emission from time-domain sources, hot plasmas in galaxy clusters and galaxies via the Sunyaev-Zeldovich effects, and dusty sources spanning from galactic star-forming regions to high-redshift star-forming galaxies. The integrated antenna-filter system provides a critical technical foundation for NEW-MUSIC’s high-performance detection capabilities.

Items.Authors: Devika K. Divakar, Phillip MacQueen, Joseph Strubhar, Andrew Pinckney
Items.Title: Design of an atmospheric dispersion corrector and double scrambler for improved fiber coupling and illumination uniformity for the HET HRS
Items.Abstract: High-precision radial velocity programs with the HET-HRS rely on exceptionally stable fiber illumination. We present the design of a new fiber-feed module integrating a static Atmospheric Dispersion Corrector and a Double Scrambler. The ADC, optimized for the HET's unique fixed-zenith-angle range, employs fixed Amici prisms to achieve chromatic correction, ensuring maximum coupling efficiency into the fiber core across the 360 - 1000 nm spectral band. We detail the optical prescription of ADC and mechanical integration within the Prime Focus Instrument Package. We also present the optical and mechanical concepts of Double Scrambler mechanism, which is a critical subsystem for minimizing the radial velocity noise by decoupling variations in input illumination from the spectrograph's output point spread function, significantly stabilizing the instrument. These two subsystems are essential for maintaining HET-HRS's stability, enabling long-term high-precision radial velocity measurements.

Items.Authors: Xianke Song, Jiahao Zhou, Yingfu Wang, Wengfei Liu, Kai Yun, Mengmeng Qian, Haoyang Zhang, Hongzhuan Hu, Jianping Wang, Jiaru Chu, Ping Zhang, Zhigang Liu, Zengxiang Zhou
Items.Title: Design of an autofocus system for a long-distance fiber view camera
Items.Abstract: To ensure the positioning accuracy of optical fibers in the Large Sky Area Multi-Object Fiber Spectroscopic Telescope (LAMOST), this study addresses focal plane deviation caused by large temperature variations in the Fiber View Camera (FVC). An autofocus system is developed, integrating an external focusing mechanism with a software algorithm that combines image clarity evaluation and hill-climbing search. The system achieves a 100% focusing success rate, effectively replaces manual focusing, and maintains both fiber positioning precision and telescope observation efficiency.

Items.Authors: Xin Luo, Baolong Chen, Qi Feng, Zhe Geng, Hong-fei Zhang, Jian Wang
Items.Title: Design of operational and test software for infrared cameras
Items.Abstract: In this paper we design and implement a camera control software system for operations of infrared cameras. The system adopts a layered architecture including an SDK for application development and a graphical client for user operations. The SDK encapsulates core interfaces such as exposure and deep cryogenic temperature control; the client provides an intuitive interface for image preview and parameter adjustment. The system is designed to meet the low-temperature and low-noise requirements of infrared observation, featuring high stability and complete logging functionality. Experimental results show that it can reliably complete camera control and data acquisition tasks.

Items.Authors: Lei Wang, Hangxin Ji, Songxin Dai, Jiahao Dong
Items.Title: Design of slit-mask for the imaging spectrometer (OASIS) of the 10-meter-class optical and infrared telescope
Items.Abstract: Design of a Slit Mask for the Imaging Spectrometer (OASIS) of a 10-Meter-Class Optical and Infrared Telescope    The Optical Astronomical Spectrograph & Imaging Subsystem (OASIS) is a first-light instrument for a 10-meter-class optical/infrared telescope, supporting multi-target spectroscopy and imaging over a 9′×3′ field of view.    The slit mask consists of thin plates distributed on a spherical surface to match the telescope focal plane, covering ~600 mm × 200 mm and accommodating hundreds of slits with customizable positions and geometries.    This work analyzes slit mask design requirements, including panel forming and slit position/shape accuracy under different observing conditions. Key factors affecting performance are evaluated, and corresponding design and fabrication strategies are proposed.

Items.Authors: Arun Surya
Items.Title: Design of the calibration system for MOIS: a multi object imaging infrared spectrograph
Items.Abstract: MOIS is a multi-object configurable slit spectrograph designed to be used with the 3.6 Devasthal Optical Telescope (DOT). It will cover the near-infrared wavelength band of 0.97 - 2.37 microns and have a spectroscopic field of view of 9’ x 3’ arc minutes. We describe the design of the calibration system for MOIS. With the large focal plane area covered by the configurable slit units, a calibration system should provide the focal plane with the same beam configuration and also match the exit port of the integrating sphere with the exit pupil of the telescope. Considering the 80 mm focal plane surface trade studies are made to understand if a scanning mode flat fielding and wavelength calibration beam would be optimal. We describe the optical design of the calibration system together with the design trades made to achieve uniformity requirements.

Items.Authors: Stéphane Schanne
Items.Title: Design of the ECLAIRs trigger for SVOM gamma-ray burst detection
Items.Abstract: The French-Chinese SVOM satellite (Space Variable Objects Monitor), launched in June 2024, with is designed to study astrophysical transient events, among which primarily Gamma-Ray Bursts (GRBs). The ECLAIRs Trigger of the hard X-ray coded-mask instrument ECLAIRs onboard SVOM autonomously localizes the bursts and requests the satellite to slew to those sources for follow-up observations by the onboard instruments MXT and VT and transmits real-time alerts to the ground, for further follow-up campaigns. This paper presents the ECLAIRs Trigger, including the design of both trigger algorithms running simultaneously onboard, the Count-Rate Trigger (CRT) and the Image Trigger (IMT). The ECLAIRs Trigger has permitted the detection of several notable GRBs, including classical as well as peculiar X-ray rich GRBs, including some high-redshift GRBs. After description of the algorithms the paper will give a summary on the most notable results obtained in flight.

Items.Authors: Meng Zhai, Qian Chen
Items.Title: Detectability of water vapor on terrestrial exoplanets around GK stars with Tianlin
Items.Abstract: China has proposed a space telescope with aperture size of 6.6 meters named Tianlin, which is dedicated for the characterization of rocky planets in the habitable zones (HZ) around nearby GK stars. It will be equipped with a low to high resolution spectrograph and a high contrast coronagraph that should allow the delivery of high quality spectrum of exoplanets. We conduct a preliminary simulation of transmission and reflected spectra for Earth-like planets around G, K type stars and perform retrieval analysis of the detectablity of H2O, a key bio-indicating molecule. Our results show that Tianlin has the ability to constrain H2O abundances in the atmosphere of Earth-like planets in most cases.

Items.Authors: Davide Vaccaro, Kenichiro Nagayoshi, Vishal Anvekar, Damian Audley, Marcel Bruijn, Jan-Willem den Herder, Jan van der Kuur, Kenichi Karatsu, Tommaso Ghigna, Peter Hargrave, Francesco Piacentini, Michele Pinchera, Giovanni Signorelli, Andrea Tartari
Items.Title: Detector development based on antenna-coupled TES bolometers with FDM readout for future space CMB instrumentation
Items.Abstract: At SRON we are developing antenna-coupled dichroic dual-polarization TES bolometers with Frequency-Domain Multiplexing (FDM) readout, with current R&D targeting the 90-150 GHz band around the CMB signal peak, with natural application to future space CMB missions such as JAXA’s LiteBIRD. We present the TES dimensioning, using a TiAu bilayer on a suspended SiN membrane, and the design trade-offs of the 4-probe antenna and bandpass filters for GHz-frequency selection based on SONNET and COMSOL simulations. We also describe the FDM readout architecture, including SRON-fabricated LC filters and VTT-developed two-stage SQUIDs. Finally, we show first characterization results of test devices fabricated at SRON towards the design optimization of the detector and readout.

Items.Authors: Georgios N. Vassilakis, Susan F. Redmond, Jason D. Rhodes, Richard J. Massey, Qiuhan He
Items.Title: Determining PSF stability requirements for low-mass dark matter subhalo detection with the Habitable Worlds Observatory
Items.Abstract: Dark matter dominates the universe's mass, yet its fundamental nature remains unknown. Competing theories predict different populations of low-mass subhalos (~10^6-10^7 M_sun), below current detection limits (~10^8 M_sun). The upcoming Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO) could reach this regime, but only if its point spread function (PSF) quality and stability are tightly controlled. We present HWO-SLAPS, a strong-lensing simulation and analysis pipeline that simulates galaxy-galaxy lenses with embedded subhalos, convolves them with a segmented-mirror PSF containing controlled aberrations and temporal drifts, and adds realistic detector noise. Using Fisher-matrix forecasts, we compute detection significance as a function of subhalo mass and PSF stability. We then map minimum detectable subhalo mass versus PSF wavefront error and drift, deriving quantitative PSF stability and engineering requirements for HWO and a general framework linking optics stability to dark-matter science yield.

Items.Authors: Roser Juanola-Parramon, Christopher Stark, Sarah Peacock, Noah Tuchow, Alex Howe, Neil Zimmerman
Items.Title: Determining the astrophysical noise floor of the Habitable Worlds Observatory’s coronagraphs
Items.Abstract: The Habitable Worlds Observatory will use a coronagraph to block starlight and reveal faint, potentially Earth-like planets around nearby stars, and to spectrally characterize them in search of oxygen, requiring SNR > 10. Achieving this science goal demands suppressing and subtracting residual starlight to a few parts in 10¹².  The challenge is often framed primarily in terms of telescope and instrument stability, the dominant engineering driver for HWO. However, many coronagraphs capable of 10⁻¹⁰ raw contrast are sensitive to details of the astrophysical scene (stellar angular diameter, hot exozodiacal dust, and starspots), which can introduce residual structure in the PSF potentially limiting starlight subtraction to levels above the required few parts in 10¹² and imposing an astrophysical, rather than instrumental, noise floor.  Here we present estimates of this astrophysical noise floor with the baselined HWO coronagraph (AAVC) and evaluate two subtraction techniques: RDI and ADI.

Items.Authors: Ivan Agostinelli, Marco Faccini, Felipe Pedreros Bustos, David Alaluf, Petr Janout, Matteo Tordi, Mauro Centrone, Lorenzo Paonni, Julienne Böttger, David Jenkins, Roberto Biasi, Laura Salvi, Roberto Speziali, Maurizio Oliviero, Andrea Di Paola
Items.Title: Development and characterization of a magneto-optical filter for daytime sodium LGS detection
Items.Abstract: Daytime detection of sodium Laser Guide Stars (LGS) is challenging due to intense and rapidly varying sky background, especially when tracking fast-moving objects such as LEO satellites and space debris. Magneto-Optical Filters (MOFs), with their ultra-narrow bandwidth and high spectral stability, offer a promising solution by providing strong suppression of unpolarized background light around the Na D₂ line. We report the development, integration, and characterization of a MOF system for the CaNaPy platform, tested in laboratory and on-sky. Results demonstrate significant background reduction and improved signal-to-noise ratio, highlighting the potential and current limitations of MOF-based spectral filtering for daytime LGS adaptive optics.

Items.Authors: Shibo Shu, Daikang Yan, Yaqiong Li, Jiamin Sun, Lin Zhu, Ye Chai, Zhouhui Liu, He Gao, Zhengwei Li, Xufang Li, Wenhao Wu, Congzhan Liu
Items.Title: Development of 6-inch detector modules for AliCPT1
Items.Abstract: AliCPT1 is a dedicated CMB polarization telescope at the northern hemisphere. The working temperature is around 300mK. The focal plane is built for 19 6-inch detector modules. In our design, each detector module has 456 pixels. We have developed both silicon-plated and metal horn arrays for this work. The beam symmetry is better than 90% and the cross-polarization is below -20dB. The TES detector array uses Al-AlMn in series. The current DRIE yield is better than 96%. To study the uniformity of the TES transition temperatures, 120 sensors have been measured. The microwave SQUID multiplexers are under development. The packaging of all components has been massively tested. Details will be presented in this talk.

Items.Authors: Yuxin Qiu, Hanzhang Wang, Ran Duan, Xiaoyun Ma, Ruirui Fan, Nannan Yue, Xiaojing Wu, Wei Duan, Fei Liu, Gang Xu
Items.Title: Development of a 5000-pixel kinetic inductance detector array for far-infrared imaging
Items.Abstract: The development of a 5000-pixel superconducting Aluminum Kinetic Inductance Detector (KID) imaging array for far-infrared astronomy (350 μm) is presented. The array features a large-scale frequency division multiplexing readout architecture with 1,000 resonators per feedline. Characterization at 50 mK demonstrates a fabrication yield greater than 95%, with intrinsic quality factors exceeding 200,000. Design strategies to minimize frequency crosstalk are discussed, alongside the resulting trade-offs in multiplexing ratios and filling factors. Future plans include the integration of feedhorn arrays and room-temperature readout electronics to establish a complete detection instrument for observational experiments.

Items.Authors: Jee-Ho Kim, Boon-Kok Tan
Items.Title: Development of a compact sideband-separating SIS mixer for the Africa Millimetre Telescope targeting 211-275 GHz
Items.Abstract: Many millimeter and sub-millimeter astronomical observatories require separating signals from different frequency sidebands to avoid spectral confusion. Traditional receivers accomplish this using waveguide components–hybrids, power splitters, directional couplers–and a set of double-sideband (DSB) superconducting mixers. At higher frequencies, however, these components become bulky, difficult to manufacture, and add loss.    We present a new compact architecture replacing most waveguide elements with modular superconducting planar-circuit chips. By re-arranging the DSB mixers and integrating waveguide components directly on-chip, we achieve full sideband separation while substantially reducing volume and complexity. We demonstrate this approach for the ALMA band 6 frequency range for the Africa Millimetre Telescope’s first-light instrument and outline its scalability to adjacent bands. Our design takes a promising step toward large multi-pixel receiver arrays for future telescopes.

Items.Authors: Jae-Hyuck Choi, Hagyong Kihm
Items.Title: Development of a deep ultraviolet Fizeau interferometer for the homogeneity evaluation of UV telescope optical materials
Items.Abstract: Calcium fluoride (CaF₂), a critical material in UV space telescopes, is known for its high transmission at short wavelengths. It has been used in various optical components such as beam splitters, grisms, and imaging windows, notably in NASA’s GALEX mission. The homogeneity of CaF₂ plays a pivotal role in optical performance, as inhomogeneities, birefringence, and crystal defects can significantly affect image quality. This study introduces a novel 193 nm interferometer for at-wavelength testing of CaF₂’s optical properties, specifically its refractive index homogeneity. Single-crystal CaF₂ samples, grown by the Czochralski method, were analyzed under both 193 nm and 633 nm wavelengths. The results show significant differences in homogeneity at 193 nm, highlighting the necessity for wavelength-specific assessments to ensure optimal performance in UV space telescopes.

Items.Authors: Shigeyuki Sako, Kazuya Matsubayashi, Yuki Hirao, Keito Kurashima, Emon Kodama, Satoshi Takita, Ryotaro Koshi, Taiga Sasaoka, Sorato Wada, Shodai Nezu, Haruka Nagasawa, Natsu Madokoro, Jin Beniyama, Kosuke Kushibiki, Takashi Miyata, Kotaro Kohno, Kentaro Motohara, Takeo Minezaki, Fumi Egusa, Itsuki Sakon, Masahiro Konishi, Hidenori Takahashi, Takafumi Kamizuka, Hiroaki Sameshima, Kana Morokuma-Matsui, Mitsuyoshi Yamagishi, Masataka Imai, Takashi Horiuchi, Natsuko M. Kato, Yuzuru Yoshii
Items.Title: Development of Laguna: an optical instrument complex for the TAO 6.5-m telescope
Items.Abstract: Laguna is an optical instrument complex being developed for installation at the bent-Cassegrain focus of the TAO 6.5-m telescope. It is designed to host multiple observational units that use different portions of a total 10-arcminute-diameter field of view (FoV). Three units are currently under development: Laguna-CAM, Laguna-SPEC, and Laguna-SPAD. Laguna-CAM is a simultaneous three-band CMOS imager with a 4-arcminute-diameter FoV. Laguna-SPEC consists of a low-dispersion prism spectrograph covering 300 to 800 nm, including the near-ultraviolet, and a medium-dispersion echelle spectrograph covering 400 to 1000 nm. Both spectrographs use slits located within the Laguna-CAM FoV. Laguna-SPAD is a high-speed polarimetric imaging unit with a 2-arcminute-diameter FoV, using a zero-readout-noise SPAD image sensor and a pair of Wollaston prisms to achieve continuous, high-speed polarimetric measurements without mechanical modulation.

Items.Authors: Damien Prêle, Sotiris Loucatos, Manuel Gonzalez, Jean-Luc Sauvageot, Xavier de la Broïse, Jean-Batiste Melin, Timothée Tollet, Gwendal Deniel
Items.Title: Development of superconducting flexible cables for cosmology and astrophysics observatories
Items.Abstract: Next-generation CMB experiments target precise B-mode measurements to probe inflation, light particles beyond the Standard Model, neutrino masses and cosmic evolution. They require thousands of TES detectors in cryogenic receivers, read out through flexible superconducting cables with minimal thermal load.  We present high-density flat niobium-based cryogenic cables for TES biasing/readout, and SQUID interconnects after multiplexing, operating deep in the superconducting transition for low residual resistance and high critical current.  Building on CEA/Irfu designs, we report recent advances from a collaboration with APC/In2p3/CNRS, SLAC, CERN and industry. A reliable process is developed using deposited Nb/NbTi layers on polyimide, fine patterning and protective coating, with bonding and cryogenic performance systematically evaluated.

Items.Authors: Yuan Liang, Jiajia Wu, Jianan Cong, Kai Zhang, Zijian Han, Zhengyang Li, Tong Zhou
Items.Title: Development of the Cassegrain focus instrument for the 1-meter telescope of Wuhan University
Items.Abstract: A Cassegrain focus instrument is developed for the 1-meter Telescope of Wuhan University. It is composed of a wide-field photometric camera and a low-resolution spectrograph to support the astronomy team at Wuhan University to study formation and evolution of galaxies, star clusters and other objects. The wide-field photometric camera can achieve image quality with FWHM ≤ 1” over a field of view of 0.44°× 0.32°. The low-resolution spectrograph has a long slit of 8’ to observe extended sources like galaxy. It can select desired spectral resolution R=1000,1500, 3000 by switching slits and cover a wide wavelength range of 400–900 nm by rotating a grism wheel. In August 2025, the instrument successfully got its first light on the Wuhan University’s 1-meter Telescope at the Lenghu astronomical site. With the commissioning observations, the instrumental performance has been further optimized and met the scientific requirements.

Items.Authors: Alessandro Poli, Marco Morsiani, Andrea Orlati, Igor Coretti, Veronica Baldini
Items.Title: Development of the digital servo system for enhanced pointing accuracy of the 32-m Gavril Grueff VLBI antenna in Medicina
Items.Abstract: High frequency observations rely critically on the stability and accuracy of a radiotelescope pointing mechanism. To establish operational autonomy and achieve higher technical performance, we initiated the independent development of a new servo system for the 32-m Grueff Antenna. Our study prioritized an empirical characterization of the telescope’s dynamics. We developed a custom drive interface allowing for high-fidelity in-situ testing. Experimental data acquired through this process highlighted critical design requirements for the system upgrade. Results demonstrate that a robust active anti-backlash torque sharing strategy is paramount to mitigate mechanical play. Furthermore, the analysis confirmed that optimal tracking precision requires strict load-to-motor inertia matching and the adoption of ultra-low cogging motors to minimize velocity ripples. Finally, the observed non-linear behaviors dictate the implementation of adaptive control architectures, such as gain scheduling.

Items.Authors: Ken Miyato, Atsushi Nishimura, Rin I. Yamada, Chieko Miyazawa, Toshikazu Takahashi, Sho Masui, Yasumasa Yamasaki, Takeshi Sakai, Ken'ichi Tatematsu, Hideo Ogawa, Toshikazu Onishi, Kazuki Tokuda, Nami Sakai
Items.Title: Development of the new 7-beam wide-band (72-116) receiver 7BEE for the Nobeyama 45m telescope
Items.Abstract: We present the development and commissioning of the new 7-beam wideband (72–116 GHz) receiver 7BEE installed on the Nobeyama 45-m telescope. The receiver enables observations in the 70 GHz band with the highest efficiency in the world for studies of the earliest phases of star formation, and also provides CO (115 GHz) observations with twice the efficiency of the former multi-beam receiver FOREST. The system incorporates wideband CLNAs and newly designed optical and RF components. The receiver noise temperatures are typically 70-90 K at the laboratory, and the system noise temperature of the 70GHz band is typically 150 K. CSV observations confirmed that the pointing, beam pattern, and overall performance meet the observatory requirements.

Items.Authors: Ye Chai, Shibo Shu, Zhouhui Liu, He Gao, Jiamin Sun, Daikang Yan, Yaqiong Li, Xufang Li, Yiwen Wang, Weijie Guo, Juexian Cao, Congzhan Liu
Items.Title: Developments of a 6-inch thermal kinetic inductance detector array for 90/150 GHz bands
Items.Abstract: The highly sensitive millimeter-wave telescope is an important tool for accurately measuring cosmic microwave background (CMB) radiation, and its core component is a detector array located in a cryogenic focal plane. The feasibility of utilizing thermal kinetic inductance detectors (TKIDs) for CMB observations has been demonstrated. To improve observation efficiency and accuracy, we propose an array of research and development of TKIDs in a 6-inch wafer for observing CMB through atmospheric windows for observations in the 90/150 GHz bands. Two pairs of probes are designed on the pixel to divide the signal into two polarization directions. Orthogonal transducer and diplexer are used for signal conversion and frequency division. 456 detector pixels will be deployed on a single array, with each pixel containing two 90 GHz and two 150 GHz detectors, for a total of 1824 detectors.

Items.Authors: Rodrigo Zeledon, Antonio Magoncelli, Matthew Gilbertson, Alain Carrier, Liz Osborne
Items.Title: Disturbance-free payload: next-generation vibration isolation technology for space-based precision-pointing missions
Items.Abstract: We present an overview of Lockheed Martin’s Disturbance-Free Payload (DFP) system in the context of its application to Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO), as well as its unique benefits over conventional vibration isolation systems. Recent advancements and enhancements to the DFP system are emphasized, including reduction of voice coil actuator noise, assessing the performance impact of cables that bridge the DFP interface, development of algorithms to handle contingency operation on orbit, fail-safe relatching mechanisms that hold the spacecraft and payload fixed during servicing of the telescope, and plans for DFP as a system to reach Technology Readiness Level (TRL) 5 by October 2029.

Items.Authors: Kevin Fanning
Items.Title: DREAMing of clear skies: impact of cloud avoidance on the LSST survey
Items.Abstract: At the end of 2023, the Dutch Rubin Enhanced Atmospheric Monitor (DREAM) was delivered to the Vera C. Rubin Observatory. This instrumentation is an all sky camera system composed of five cameras imaging in braodband optical. This system produces transparency maps of the sky based on brightness fluctuations of stars observed by DREAM. This poster will briefly introduce the DREAM system, its constructions and pipelines, including some validations of transparency maps with on sky LSSTCam imaging. This poster will conclude with work demonstrating the impact of a cloud avoidance scheme in the Vera C. Rubin Observatory’s LSST using a year’s worth of real transparency maps from Cerro Pachon in simulated LSST surveys. While the Rubin Observatory undertakes LSST, it has immense flexibility in selecting telescope pointing providing a compelling test of how integrating transparency maps into robotic telescopes can impact efficiency.

Items.Authors: Nathan Amouroux, Parker Fagrelius, Thibault Guillemin, Fritz Mueller, Jérémy Neveu, Eli Rykoff, Elana Urbach
Items.Title: Early throughput results from the collimated beam projector at the Vera C. Rubin Observatory
Items.Abstract: The Vera C. Rubin Observatory’s LSST requires accurate photometric calibration to meet its science goals, particularly for cosmological measurements using Type Ia supernovae. The Collimated Beam Projector (CBP) has been developed to support this effort by emulating monochromatic point sources of known wavelength and flux to enable direct throughput measurements of the telescope system. Initial results demonstrate the capability in determining the instrumental response of the Simonyi Telescope and in characterizing LSSTCam filters throughput. The CBP also enables detailed mapping of shifts in filter bandpass edges across the focal plane, which can vary by several nanometers with angle of incidence. These early results validate the CBP as a powerful calibration tool and establish the foundation for ongoing photometric throughput monitoring throughout LSST operations.

Items.Authors: Talia Saeid, Reinier M. Janssen, Hessel Schulte, Steve Hailey-Dunsheath, Shubh Agrawal, James E. Aguirre, Justin S. Bracks, Charles M. Bradford, Brockton S. Brendal, Jeffrey P. Filippini, Jianyang Fu, Karolina Garcia, Christopher E. Groppi, Dylan Joralmon, Garrett Keating, Ryan P. Keenan, Lun-Jun Liu, Ian N. Lowe, Alex Manduca, Daniel P. Marrone, Philip D. Mauskopf, Evan C. Mayer, Sydnee O'Donnell, Simon Tartakovsky, Mathilde Van Cuyck, Joaquin D. Vieira, Jessica A. Zebrowski
Items.Title: Effects of magnetic fields on the kinetic inductance detector arrays for the Terahertz Intensity Mapper
Items.Abstract: Kinetic Inductance Detectors (KIDs) are superconducting micro-resonators used for radiation detection. KIDs are widely applied in fields such as astrophysics, cosmology, remote sensing, and quantum computing. Managing the quality factor (Q) and minimizing frequency scatter are crucial in optimizing KID arrays. Deviations of up to 1% can reduce yield or disrupt frequency-to-position correlation, limiting the array's scientific capabilities. Low Q values also decrease detector sensitivity. We present the impact of magnetic fields on quality factor and frequency scatter in a KID array used in the Terahertz Intensity Mapper, aiming to optimize KIDs for diverse applications.

Items.Authors: Elia Costa, Andrea Baruffolo, Alessandro Ballone, Andrea Balestra, Daphne Diretto, Salvatore Lampitelli, Alessandro Lorenzetto, Benedetta Di Francesco, Angelie Alagao, David Barr, Bernardo Salasnich, Aurelie Magniez
Items.Title: EKARUS at Asiago Observatory: Design and Implementation of the Instrument Control Software
Items.Abstract: The EKARUS project is a collaboration between LAM, ONERA, INAF, Durham University, and IPAG, aiming at bringing the Papyrus AO test bench at the 1.8m telescope of the Asiago Observatory. This paper details the design and implementation of the EKARUS Instrument Control Software (ICS), which is based on the PLICO Python framework. The architecture utilizes a distributed, service-oriented model, leveraging ZeroMQ (ZMQ) for communication between a central component “Sequencer like” and specialized hardware servers. A key design principle is strict hardware abstraction, this is a significant advantage for an R&D test bench as it guarantees high flexibility and rapid component upgrade cycles. The core work involves extending PLICO to integrate custom hardware. This modular architecture delivers strong adaptability and efficient support for the EKARUS AO bench infrastructure and its interface with the Real-Time Controller (RTC) and the Telescope Control System (TCS).

Items.Authors: Matteo Menessini, Lorenzo Busoni, Cédric Taïssir Héritier, Vincent Chambouleyron, Carmelo Arcidiacono, Luca Cortese, Davide Greggio
Items.Title: EKARUS at Asiago Observatory: simulations and performance analysis of a modular XAO system
Items.Abstract: EKARUS is a highly-modular R&D platform to be installed next year at Asiago, providing a SCAO correction with a first stage operating in the visible and a second stage operating in the near IR, including a pupil fragmentation unit to inject segment phasing errors. We performed simulations to determine the performance and the optimal loop parameters for different observing conditions, for both single and dual stage configurations. We analysed the robustness of the AO loop parameters to different disturbances, including actuator mis-registration errors, NCPAs and pyramid WFS glass imperfections. In particular, we studied the sensitivity to the introduction of a differential piston, comparing wavefront sensing methods fusing data from sensors operating at different wavelengths, in the first and second stage.   Simulation results are used to select the best options during the system's optical design and will provide key insights for on-sky performance optimizan of the on-sky performance.

Items.Authors: Adam K. Taras, Barnaby Norris, Christopher Betters, Daniel Dahl, Nathan Long, Andrew Ross-Adams, Peter G. Tuthill, Jin Wei, Sergio Leon-Saval
Items.Title: Empirical spectro-polarimetric characterisation of photonic lanterns
Items.Abstract: Photonic lanterns efficiently map input spatial modes to single-mode outputs for applications like high angular resolution imaging and nulling interferometry. However, manufacturing limits prevent full control over the device's mode transfer matrix at the design stage, making empirical characterization essential.   We present a system that directly measures the electric field of a photonic lantern's principal modes using digital off-axis holography over a 73nm range near 1550nm and in two orthogonal polarizations, unambiguously determining the device's transfer matrix. This is the first multi-wavelength, polarization-decomposed characterization.   Applying this to a 19-port lantern, we found significant differences from simulations in wavelength evolution rate and relative dispersion. Our results highlight the importance of measuring the as-fabricated device and we share the empirical transfer matrices to enable future astrophotonic design.

Items.Authors: Mikołaj Kałuszyński, Marek Górski, Mirosław Kicia
Items.Title: End-to-end operations at OCM multi-telescope observatory: from scheduling to real-time light curves with TACOSS platform
Items.Abstract: The Rolf Chini Cerro Murphy Observatory (OCM) operates a heterogeneous fleet of telescopes (0.6m–2.5m) simultaneously with a minimal on-site team. To maximize scientific throughput without inflating staffing costs, OCM implemented a unified, operator-centric control paradigm, moving beyond traditional single-instrument silos. This operational model is enabled by TACOSS, a framework utilizing service-oriented architecture and persistent-queue messaging to decouple observing logic from diverse hardware.  This design streamlines the workflow from dynamic scheduling to real-time scientific results, including calibrated spectra and high-precision light curves. It bridges the gap between rigid robotic automation and the flexibility required for complex campaigns. Proven at OCM, TACOSS provides a scalable solution for facilities ranging from educational setups to large scientific arrays, ensuring resilience and efficiency in modern observatory operations.

Thompson, Calvin Tsai, Carole Tucker, Anthony D. Turner, Clara Vergès, Abigail G. Vieregg, Albert Wandui, Alexis C. Weber, Don Wiebe, Justin Willmert, Wai Ling K. Wu, Hung-I Yang, Cyndia Yu, Lingzhen Zeng, Cheng Zhang, Silvia Zhang
Items.Title: Engineering of titanium transition edge sensor wafers for the BA4 receiver of BICEP Array
Items.Abstract: BA4-90/150, the fourth receiver in the BICEP Array series, is a dichroic 90/150 GHz instrument targeting the frequency space where sensitivity to the CMB polarization is maximized and is central to achieving σ(r) on the order of 0.001 with SPT delensing. Set for deployment in the 2026–2027 austral summer, it is projected to be the most sensitive receiver in the experiment deployed to date and introduces key innovations requiring tighter control of systematics, including optical and electrical crosstalk. Prototype titanium transition edge sensor wafers aim to reduce noise and inform the final integrated wafer for full receiver commissioning.

Items.Authors: Jayke S. Nguyen, Charlotte Guthery, Jacob Taylor, Antonin Bouchez, Jaren Ashcraft, Quinn Konopacky
Items.Title: Enhanced image sharpening for Keck AO using gradient-based phase retrieval techniques
Items.Abstract: Image sharpening corrects for the non-common path aberrations (NCPA) on adaptive optics systems and is an important step for adaptive optics calibration each night. The current image sharpening algorithm implemented on Keck uses focus diversity paired with a Gerchberg-Saxton phase retrieval algorithm. Implemented in IDL, this code has been in use since the beginning of adaptive optics on Keck. While the current workhorse algorithm works well, gradient-based phase retrieval methods have been shown to converge faster to a lower wavefront error. We present results from using a new and improved Python-based image sharpening code on the Keck AO bench and show an improvement in the convergence time over the old image sharpening algorithm, reducing the overall time needed for calibrations. Since it is not possible to show a “ground truth” for NCPA correction we instead compare our image sharpening algorithm to archival data and show that it converges to a similar solution.

Items.Authors: Ju Guan
Items.Title: EP-FXT source search software: quick-look database construction and source catalog generation
Items.Abstract: The Einstein Probe (EP) is a space X-ray mission for time-domain astrophysics, aiming to discover high-energy transients and monitor variable objects. Its principal payload, Follow-up X-ray Telescope (FXT), performs prompt/deep follow-up of EP-WXT-triggered targets and characterizes X-ray transients. Due to rapid fading/evolution of transient signals, fast and reliable FXT data analysis is critical for their discovery and timely follow-up to determine source nature. We thus developed a real-time source search toolkit that automatically processes EP-FXT observations. The toolkit generates a continuously updated quick-look database with: 1) source products (position, count rate, flux, etc.); 2) identified transients/bursts; 3) source lists; 4) sky maps. Based on this comprehensive quick-look database, we constructed the EP-FXT source catalog and analyzed the source properties statistically.

Items.Authors: Jorge Quintero-Nehrkorn, Fernando Merlos-García, Josué Barrera Martín, Ángela Hernández-Delgado, Miguel Nuñez, Mary Barreto Cabrera
Items.Title: EST Safety System
Items.Abstract: The European Solar Telescope (EST) requires a comprehensive, multi-layer Safety System capable of ensuring the protection of personnel, equipment, and the telescope infrastructure under a wide range of operational and environmental conditions. As part of the recent Preliminary Design Review (PDR), the EST Safety System architecture has been evaluated in terms of functional completeness, hardware and software feasibility, subsystem interfaces, and overall integration with the EST Control System.    This paper presents the current design of the EST Safety System, which adopts a hierarchical approach combining hardwired industrial safety logic implemented through PLCs with high-level software monitoring and supervision. The system encompasses hazard detection, interlock management, emergency stop coordination, and safe-state transitions for all telescope subsystems, including telescope structure, optics, instruments, thermal systems, and access facilities.

Items.Authors: Pierre Jouve, Thierry Fusco, Benoit Neichel, Carlos Correia
Items.Title: Estimation of full-aperture uplink tip-tilt in laser guide star systems using spatial diversity and machine learning
Items.Abstract: Laser guide star adaptive optics systems greatly expand sky coverage for large telescopes but remain limited by their inability to sense uplink tip-tilt (TT), as no absolute reference exists at infinity. Low-order aberrations must therefore be obtained from natural guide stars (NGSs), constraining performance. Recent data-driven methods offer new ways to extract subtle information hidden in AO telemetry. We present a framework that exploits spatial diversity in a monostatic launch using a full-aperture 50-cm laser beam, combined with machine-learning inference, to estimate uplink TT directly from the LGS. The method reveals information previously inaccessible in LGS wavefront measurements. Under controlled conditions with a single layer and noiseless measurement, the model is able to retrieve 90% of the TT signal. With dual-layer turbulence with noisy measurements, it recovers up to 60% of the uplink signal. These results establish a clear proof of concept for uplink TT estimation.

Items.Authors: Max Braun, Scott C. Roberts, Keivan Ahmadi, Peter Byrnes, Joeleff Fitzsimmons, Taz Oldaker, John Rogers
Items.Title: Evaluating the suitability of MEMS and piezoelectric based accelerometers for use in measuring structural vibration in astronomical telescopes and instruments
Items.Abstract: We describe the development of an instrumented test-bed, including structure, optics and accelerometers, for experimental validation of integrated modeling results. We utilize integrated modeling tools to predict the optical response of the test-bed given a generated disturbance from a modal shaker. The integrated model uses the measured accelerations on the structure to predict the structural dynamics of the system and the resulting optical degradation. The actual optical degradation is measured with a wavefront sensor at the output of the optical system. While piezoelectric accelerometers are more sensitive, and have a lower noise floor, the cost advantage of MEMS-based accelerometers makes them attractive candidates. We present measurements of the performance of various accelerometers and estimate the error in measurement of each type against a typical vibration environment for our test-bed and for typical use cases on astronomical telescopes and instrumentation.

Items.Authors: Fabian Haberhauer, Oliver Czoske, Hugo Buddelmeijer, Kieran Leschinski, Janus Brink, Werner Zeilinger
Items.Title: Evolving ScopeSim: An integrated online exposure simulator for the ELT
Items.Abstract: The European Extremely Large Telescope (ELT) demands modern, high-fidelity observation simulation tools capable of handling its complex optical and adaptive optics systems. ScopeSim, developed at the University of Vienna, already provides realistic simulations for several ELT instruments, but its current deployment is limited to local installations, and is mostly used by instrument consortium members. We present its expansion into a scalable, web-based service designed to support the broader ELT/VLT community. The platform will offer validated instrument packages, visualization tools, and consistent feedback mechanisms for astronomers, proposal reviewers, and observatory staff. This development addresses a critical gap in current observation-planning infrastructure and provides a flexible, future-proof solution for next-generation observatories.

Items.Authors: Marina Rejkuba, Nelma Alas Silva, Thomas Bierwirth, Henri M. J. Boffin, Stéphane Brillant, Olivier Hainaut, Maksym Korpan, Ferdinando Patat, Michael Pruemm, Michael F. Sterzik, Alexander Weiss, Markus Wittkowski
Items.Title: Evolving time allocation and scheduling for the ESO VLT and VLTI
Items.Abstract: The European Southern Observatory (ESO) has transitioned its main Call for Proposals from a 6-monthly to a yearly cadence. To complement this change, ESO is introducing a new Fast Track Channel, designed to support observing proposals motivated by emerging scientific opportunities that require a response on a timescale of a few months. These changes necessitated substantial updates to ESO’s time allocation and scheduling processes, as well as the underlying software tools. We present the evolution of ESO’s scheduling framework that simultaneously accommodates scientific observations and technical time requests. The system incorporates novel concepts for managing commitments across overlapping cycles and accounting for the remaining science fraction from previously accepted proposals. New science proposals and new or updated technical time requests are scheduled within the same optimisation environment. The scheduler includes the joint optimisation of multiple telescope schedules.

Items.Authors: Barbara Pedroni, David F. Buscher, Eugene B. Seneta
Items.Title: Exploring advanced control strategies for Fast Tip-Tilt correction at the MROI
Items.Abstract: The Magdalena Ridge Observatory Interferometer (MROI) will achieve angular resolutions down to 0.6 mas in the optical and near-infrared wavebands. Most of the corrupting influence of the atmosphere on the incoming wavefronts is removed by a Fast Tip-Tilt system at each unit telescope. Closed-loop control algorithms and centroid estimation techniques to enhance its performance are explored. These include Kalman filter-based predictors and machine learning approaches to estimate the centroid of speckle-corrupted images.

Items.Authors: Tommaso Ghigna, Jiao Ding, Yu Zhou, Ryota Hayakawa, Kaori Hattori
Items.Title: Fabrication and characterization of Ti/Au thin films for TES applications
Items.Abstract: We report on developing and characterizing Ti/Au bilayer films for Transition-Edge Sensors, fabricated by e-beam evaporation at OIST. Au thickness was varied from 0 to 6 times the Ti thickness, while Ti was fixed at 30 nm. Test structures covering the full Au/Ti range were patterned to study how composition affects superconducting and normal-state behavior. We present measurements of the transition temperature (Tc), its dependence on Au/Ti ratio, and Tc uniformity across wafers. We also report resistance-per-square (R□) and its spatial scatter, revealing film homogeneity, interface quality, and process reproducibility. The results show controllable tuning of Tc and normal-state properties through bilayer engineering, enabling tailored TES performance. We conclude with relevance to bolometers, X-ray microcalorimeters, and emerging optical single-photon TES devices, and outline next steps toward integrating these films into full detector architectures.

Items.Authors: Dohoon Kim, Il kweon Moon, Hyukson Kwon, Gisung Park, Yunjong Kim, Jongwan Ko, JaeYeong Jo, Taejong Kim, Minho Seo, Young-Soo Kim
Items.Title: Fabrication and metrology of off-axis freeform mirrors for the K-DRIFT G1 telescope
Items.Abstract: We fabricated and tested three freeform mirrors for the KASI Deep Rolling Imaging Fast Telescope, a confocal off-axis three-mirror system with a 300 mm entrance pupil diameter. To reduce weight, lightweighting design was applied to the primary and tertiary mirrors, resulting in weight reductions of 73.2 % and 73.9 %, respectively. The secondary mirror (SM) was not subject to the lightweighting process. Surface profiles were measured using Coordinate Measuring Machines (CMMs) during grinding. For polishing and finishing, CGH was used for the primary and tertiary mirrors (PM, TM), while LuphoScan was used for the secondary mirror (SM). All mirrors met the required surface accuracy of 20 nm RMS and 100 nm PV.

Items.Authors: David J. Thoen, Dimitry Lamers, Martijn Veen, Daniela Perez Capelo, Marcel P. Bruijn, Tonny H. M. Coppens, Arno Gotink, Ton J. van der Linden, Kenichiro Nagayoshi, Vishal Anvekar, Rene A. van der Windt, Paolo M. Sberna, Shahab O. Dabironezare, Jochem J. A. Baselmans
Items.Title: Fabrication development for the lens-antenna coupled and lens-absorber coupled kinetic inductance detector arrays for PRIMAger
Items.Abstract: PRIMA is a next generation far-infrared space telescope, with cryogenically cooled optics, coupling to ultrasensitive lens-coupled microwave kinetic inductance detector (MKID) arrays. In this paper we explain the detailed fabrication procedure of the lens-antenna and lens-absorber coupled detectors for the PRIMA Polarimetric Imager (PPI) and PRIMA Hyperspectral Imager (PHI), respectively. Emphasis will be placed on the aluminium preparation, patterning and its step coverage. We elaborate on how we make the fabrication reliable and exactly to specification with thousands of membranes and detectors on a single 100 mm diameter wafer.

Items.Authors: Kosuke Kushibiki, Kentaro Motohara, Tadayuki Kodama, Masayuki Akiyama, Yosuke Minowa, Yusei Koyama, Ichi Tanaka, Kumiko Morihana, Kenshi Yanagisawa, Sadman Ali, Takashi Hattori, Michitoshi Yoshida, Masahiro Konishi, Shiang-Yu Wang
Items.Title: Final design of Wide Field Imager (WFI) for ULTIMATE-Subaru
Items.Abstract: Wide Field Imager (WFI) is a near-infrared (0.9–2.5 μm) imager which covers a wide field of view and samples high-spatial resolution realized by a new Ground Layer Adaptive Optics system of the Subaru telescope, called ULTIMATE-Subaru delivering 0.2" image quality in the K-band over a 20' field of view (FoV).     To cover its wide FoV, WFI consists of four identical optical units, each covering a 6.8′ x 6.8′ FoV, for a total FoV of 13.6′ x 13.6′. Each unit accommodates up to 20 filters, including broad-, medium-, and narrow-band filters, and to operate a larger number of filters, narrow-band filters are designed to be easily exchangeable. A HAWAII-4RG detector with 0.1″/pixel sampling is used per unit.     WFI has passed the final design and now moves to the fabrication phase. In this presentation, we will describe the WFI’s specifications, technical details, and current development status.

Items.Authors: Alexander Díaz, Gaizka Murga, Santiago Royo, Maialen González, Noel Rodrigo, Jon Blanco, Jon Ander Paniagua, Joseba Blázquez, Andreas Förster, Sebastian Schmid, Philippe Gitton, Samuel Lévêque, Martin Dimmler
Items.Title: Final integration and testing for the Extremely Large Telescope (ELT) M1 Local Coherencer
Items.Abstract: The 39m primary mirror of the ELT is composed of 798 hexagonal segments. These are regularly replaced for recoating and have to be phased again. The Local Coherencer is a non-contact metrology system aimed to assist in the phasing of a target segment. The system simultaneously measures the relative pistons on the six sides of this segment with respect to neighbouring ones with an accuracy below 300nm (2 sigma) in a range of ±0.25mm using a patented partially coherent light interferometer.    The system has been produced, integrated, and thoroughly tested to demonstrate performance, even under different environmental conditions such as, gravity orientation, operational temperatures and external lighting conditions. To comply with performance requirements mathematical compensation models have been developed for some effects, such as temperature, gravity orientation and repeatable non-linearities.    This paper presents the final integration of the system and the acceptance testing results.
